samples.xml_description:
<module id="fsm">
    <description>Mealy FSM Detection Circuit</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="IN">Input signal to be detected.</input>
        <input id="CLK">Clock signal for synchronization.</input>
        <input id="RST">Reset signal to initialize the FSM.</input>
        <output id="MATCH">Output signal indicating a match condition.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="S0">Initial state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S1">State after detecting '1'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S2">State after detecting '00'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S3">State after detecting '0011'. This constant represents the final state where the pattern is detected.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <signal id="next_state" type="reg" width="3">Next state register.</signal>
        <signal id="state" type="reg" width="3">Current state register.</signal>
        <assign next_state = (state == S0 && IN == 1) ? S1 :
                            (state == S1 && IN == 0) ? S2 :
                            (state == S2 && IN == 1) ? S3 :
                            (state == S3 && IN == 1) ? S3 : S0;
        
        <always @(posedge CLK or posedge RST)>
            if(RST)
                state <= S0;
            else
                state <= next_state;
        end
        
        <assign MATCH = ((state == S3) && (IN == 1)) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>
        The FSM operates based on the current state and the input signal IN. On each rising edge of the clock or when reset is asserted, the state transitions according to the predefined state machine logic. The MATCH signal is generated based on the current state and the input signal IN. It asserts HIGH when the pattern is detected, specifically when the current state is S3 and the input signal IN is 1. Otherwise, it asserts LOW.
    </implementation>
</module>
